summary: An excerpt from a fiction work (Book 10, part 150) in which Ria explains to Leon how a large sum was spent on quieting the skies: fake consumer-protection lawsuits forced recalls of loud jetpacks, which were rebuilt with engineered quiet pipes. She insists the scheme avoided bribery and assassination and frames the money as a means of directing power. The scene then shifts to a rooftop co-op bar where Ria, a member who worked off her membership by planting trees and a mint garden, discusses her wealth with Leon.
one_line: Ria explains to Leon how a billion-scale project quieted city jetpacks through staged lawsuits, then they drink daiquiris on a rooftop co-op.
key_facts: Ria says the company dummied-up consumer-protection lawsuits that 'forced' the recall of loud jetpacks.
The recalled jetpacks were rebuilt with pipes engineered and tuned for quieter flight.
Ria says Viktor spent about eight billion in the end on the quieting project.
Ria says the sums are 'meaningless' and that 'Power is what matters.'
Ria says the group does not use assassination, and Leon's joke about Viktor ninjas offing a jetpack rider falls flat.
Ria describes the approach as 'sweet' and says everyone got what they wanted: fast rides, quiet skies, safe, cheap vehicles.
An old school jetpack flyer is described as loud as the inside of an ice-blender and is said to be machining his own replacement parts because no one makes them anymore.
The rooftop conservatory bar serves daiquiris made with limes picked from trees on the roof.
The barman inspects several limes before twisting off a basket's worth and juicing them over his blender.
Membership at the rooftop bar is not for sale; members must work it off because it is a co-op.
Ria says she planted the whole row of trees on the roof.
Ria says she also planted the mint garden, which has a small stream winding through rocks.
Leon guesses that Ria must earn a lot of money, and she responds unembarrassed, waggling her eyebrows.
